science.qualification: Photosphere color from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum, dimmed toward the limb by the quadratic law Claret & Bloemen (2011), A&A 529, A75 compute from ATLAS model atmospheres for the Johnson V band at 5,995 K and log g 4.45 (u1 0.416, u2 0.286): a model, because no fit of this star's limb is used. The disc is unresolved: no map or absolute brightness is implied. Self-luminous, so no lighting.

science.label: Sector 10
science.description: Brightness of the star's surface that reproduces its light as it turns once in 2.99 days, fitted with starry to the TESS mission's own 2-minute light curve of sector 10 (its PDC-MAP flux) (the light varies by 2.6%; the map's curve leaves a scatter of 0.21%, the light's own noise being 0.04%). A light curve fixes how bright each longitude is, not the latitude of what darkens it. In this sector the method of Holcomb et al. (2022, ApJ 936, 138) finds a period of 3.10 d from the autocorrelation, whose peaks have a height of 0.42, a width of 0.42 and a fit of 0.94, and in all 7 of the star's sectors together a period of 2.99 d from the autocorrelation, whose peaks have a height of 0.63, a width of 0.43 and a fit of 0.99; its criteria accept that as the star's rotation. The map is made at a tilt of 70°, worked out from the star's rotation speed, period and radius. Gaia DR3 lists 142 other stars within 63 arcseconds, with 23% of their light and the star's together. A reduction made in this project, not a published map.
science.title: TESS · brightness map made here · Sector 10

science.label: Color + brightness
science.description: The star's color (#fff3f4, its Color dataset) over the brightness map this project made from the star's light in TESS sector 90 (March and April 2025): the map's scale, 96% to 104% of the mean surface, runs from a darker, richer tone of the same hue to the color itself. The contrast is drawn far stronger than it is, so the parts can be told apart: the darkest part gives 6.1% less light than the brightest. Longitudes are fixed by the light curve; latitudes and shapes are not. No color change of the spots is drawn: none is measured. A reduction made in this project, not a published map.
science.title: TESS · the star in its color over its brightness map · March and April 2025
